# SVG to Slides — editable SVGs in Google Slides

SVG to Slides is a free Chrome extension that inserts SVG files into Google Slides as native, editable shapes.

Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

- Install: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter (no install): https://svgslid.es/convert
- Google Slides add-on: https://svgslid.es/addon

## The problem
Google Slides doesn't support SVG files. Your options are to flatten them into PNGs or take the long way through EMF conversion, Google Drawings, and copy-paste.

## What it does
- **Edit individual elements.** Every SVG path becomes its own Slides shape. Recolour any element with the standard fill picker.
- **Resize without losing quality.** From a small footer icon to a full-slide graphic, every edge stays sharp.
- **Use SVGs in your themes.** Add converted graphics to theme layouts and reuse them across slides.

## How it works
1. Install the extension from the Chrome Web Store. No account required.
2. Open Google Slides, in any existing or new presentation.
3. Drag in your SVG. Its paths become editable shapes.

## Limits
- Gradients come through in the online converter; in the extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.
- Arc commands (A/a) are converted into smooth curves.
- Up to 25 files per drop in the extension; use the online converter for larger batches.

## Questions
### Can you upload or import an SVG file into Google Slides?
Not as an editable graphic. Google Slides doesn't support SVG files. Install SVG to Slides and drag the file onto a slide, or convert it online at svgslid.es/convert. Every path arrives as a native Slides shape.

### How is this different from Microsoft PowerPoint?
PowerPoint can insert an SVG file and convert it to shapes. Google Slides can't. SVG to Slides gives Slides the same result: vector graphics you can select, recolour, and resize.

### Can I add SVG icons to Google Slides?
Yes. Drag up to 25 SVG icons onto a slide at once. Each one becomes editable shapes with no background box, so you can recolour it to match your theme.

### Do the shapes stay sharp when I resize them?
Yes. They're vector graphics, so a small footer icon and a full-slide graphic both keep crisp edges.

### Can I use SVG logos in my Google Slides theme?
Yes. Add converted logos and icons to your theme layouts and reuse them across slides. The shapes also work in Google Drawings.

### Is it free?
Yes. Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

## Privacy
The Chrome extension converts on your device with an embedded WebAssembly engine; your file usually never leaves the browser. Details: https://svgslid.es/privacy


---

# SVG to Google Slides converter (online)

Upload SVG files at https://svgslid.es/convert and get a Slides-ready file in Google Drive with real, editable vector shapes.

1. Upload one or more .svg files. Each SVG becomes one slide.
2. Every `<path>` becomes its own native, individually selectable shape in Google Slides, not a flattened image.
3. The file is uploaded to Google Drive and a link is returned, optionally shared to a Google account you provide.

- Links are deleted after 7 days. To keep a file, open it in Drive and choose File → Make a copy.
- Solid fills, strokes and gradients come through. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves.

Working in a deck already? The free Chrome extension drops SVGs straight onto a slide: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

# SVG vs PNG in Google Slides™

When Google Slides flattens an SVG it becomes a single image that blurs when resized and can't be recoloured or edited. SVG to Slides converts every path into Slides' own native shape format instead, so the result behaves like a shape you drew yourself.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Flattened vs. converted

| Pasted as PNG (default) | Inserted with SVG to Slides |
|---|---|
| Blurs or pixelates when resized | Resizes at any size, always crisp |
| One flattened image, single object | Every path is its own selectable shape |
| Can't recolour without re-exporting | Recolour any shape directly in Slides |
| Can't animate individual elements | Animate each shape independently |
| Can't edit points or paths | Right-click → Edit points, like any native shape |

## Pick your route
- **Chrome extension** — Drag an SVG file straight onto an open Slides tab and drop it in place. No dialog, no upload step. (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi)
- **Web Uploader** — Upload one or more SVGs and get back a Google Drive link to a ready-made Slides file, one slide per SVG. (https://svgslid.es/convert)
- **Google Slides add-on** — Insert SVGs into a presentation you're already editing, from a dialog inside Slides itself. (https://svgslid.es/addon)

## How it stays a vector
- Every <path> in your SVG is converted directly into Google Slides' own native shape format. It isn't re-rendered as an image and it isn't a third-party embed.
- The result behaves exactly like a shape you drew in Slides yourself: resizable, recolourable, editable.

## Questions

### Does Google Slides support SVG natively?
Not as an editable format. Slides rasterizes an inserted SVG into a flattened image, so you lose the ability to edit individual paths or recolour parts of it. SVG to Slides converts it into Slides' native shape format instead, so it stays fully editable.

### What happens to gradients and complex curves?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.

### Is my file uploaded anywhere?
Depends on the surface. The Chrome extension converts entirely on your device using an embedded WebAssembly engine, so your file usually never leaves the browser. The online converter and add-on send the file to our backend for conversion. See the privacy policy for specifics.

### Is it free?
Yes. Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

# How to insert an SVG into Google Slides™

Google Slides doesn't support SVG files, so you can't upload one as an editable graphic. To insert an SVG into Google Slides, install the free SVG to Slides Chrome extension, open your presentation, and drag the .svg file onto a slide. Each path becomes its own native Slides shape.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## How to do it
1. **Install the free Chrome extension.** Add SVG to Slides from the Chrome Web Store. No account required.
2. **Open your presentation in Google Slides.** Any existing or new deck.
3. **Drag the SVG file onto a slide.** Click to place it, then press ⌘/Ctrl + V. Its paths become editable shapes. Up to 25 SVG files per drop.

## Every way to get an SVG into Google Slides

| Method | Result in Slides | What it takes |
|---|---|---|
| SVG to Slides Chrome extension | Editable shapes, one per path | Drag and drop onto the slide |
| SVG to Slides web uploader | Editable shapes, one slide per SVG | Upload in the browser, open the Google Drive link |
| SVG to Slides add-on | Editable shapes | Extensions menu inside Google Slides |
| Convert to PNG, then Insert → Image | One flattened image that blurs when resized | Any image converter |
| EMF or WMF via Google Drawings | Shapes, after several manual steps | A converter, Google Drive, Google Drawings |
| Microsoft PowerPoint, then import | Shapes, after a round trip through Drive | A PowerPoint licence |

## Import an SVG without installing anything
- Web uploader. Upload one or more SVG files at svgslid.es/convert and get a Google Drive link to a Slides-ready file, one slide per SVG. Good for bulk conversion.
- Google Slides add-on. Insert SVGs from a dialog inside Slides, without leaving the tab. Get the add-on.

## Insert SVG icons into Google Slides
- Download icons as SVG files from any icon library and drag them onto your slide, up to 25 per drop.
- Each icon arrives as native shapes with no background box, so you can recolour it with the fill picker to match your theme.
- For a whole icon set, upload it at svgslid.es/convert and get one slide per icon, ready to copy from.

## The manual workaround: EMF and Google Drawings
1. Convert the SVG to an EMF or WMF file with a desktop or online converter.
2. Upload the EMF or WMF file to Google Drive.
3. Open it with Google Drawings.
4. Copy the shapes and paste them into your Google Slides presentation.
It works, but it's four steps for every file.

## The Microsoft PowerPoint route
1. In PowerPoint, choose Insert → Pictures and pick the SVG file.
2. Right-click the graphic and choose Convert to Shape.
3. Save the presentation as .pptx and upload it to Google Drive.
4. Open it with Google Slides and copy the shapes into your deck.
It needs a PowerPoint licence and a round trip through Drive for every graphic.

## Questions

### How do I import an SVG into Google Slides?
Install the free SVG to Slides Chrome extension and drag the SVG file onto a slide, or upload it at svgslid.es/convert. Both turn every path into a native, editable Slides shape.

### Can I upload an SVG to Google Slides directly?
Not as an editable graphic. Without a converter, your options are to flatten it into a PNG or take the long way through EMF conversion, Google Drawings, and copy-paste. SVG to Slides converts the file into native Slides shapes instead.

### Can I insert SVG icons into Google Slides?
Yes. Drag up to 25 SVG icons onto a slide at once. Each one becomes editable shapes you can recolour and resize without losing quality.

### How many SVGs can I insert at once?
Up to 25 per drop with the Chrome extension. For larger batches, use the bulk converter at svgslid.es/convert.

### Does it cost anything?
Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

### Is my file uploaded anywhere?
The Chrome extension converts on your device using an embedded WebAssembly engine, so your file usually never leaves the browser. The web converter and add-on send the file to our backend for conversion.

# Does Google Slides™ support SVG?

No. Google Slides doesn't keep SVG files as editable vectors. Your options are to flatten the SVG into a PNG, or convert it through EMF and Google Drawings. SVG to Slides converts the file into Slides' native shape format, so it stays editable.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Flattened vs. converted

| Pasted as PNG (default) | Inserted with SVG to Slides |
|---|---|
| Blurs or pixelates when resized | Resizes at any size, always crisp |
| One flattened image, single object | Every path is its own selectable shape |
| Can't recolour without re-exporting | Recolour any shape directly in Slides |
| Can't animate individual elements | Animate each shape independently |
| Can't edit points or paths | Right-click → Edit points, like any native shape |

## Questions

### Can you import an SVG into Google Slides?
Not as editable vector shapes. Install the SVG to Slides Chrome extension and drag the file onto a slide, or upload it at svgslid.es/convert. Both turn every path into a native Slides shape.

### Why does my SVG look blurry in Google Slides?
It's been flattened into a raster image, so it pixelates when you resize it. Converted with SVG to Slides, it stays a vector and every edge stays sharp.

### What happens to gradients and complex curves?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Pick your route
- **Chrome extension** — Drag an SVG straight onto an open Slides tab and drop it in place. No dialog, no upload step. Converts in your browser. (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi)

The link stays active for 7 days. To keep a file, open it in Drive and choose File → Make a copy. The copy is fully yours, with no expiry.

### Is it really free?
Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

# Edit and recolor SVGs in Google Slides™

Once converted with SVG to Slides, every path in your SVG is a separate native Slides shape. Select one element and change its fill with the standard picker, edit its points, or animate it on its own.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## What you can do
- **Select individual elements.** Every path is its own selectable shape, not one flattened image.
- **Recolour with the fill picker.** Change any shape's colour directly in Slides. No re-exporting.
- **Edit points.** Right-click → Edit points, like any shape you drew yourself.
- **Animate each shape.** Build transitions element by element instead of animating one image.

## Questions

### Can I change the color of an SVG in Google Slides?
Yes, once it's converted. SVG to Slides turns each path into a native shape, so you can recolour any element with the standard fill picker.

### Can I edit the points of an SVG shape?
Yes. Right-click a converted shape and choose Edit points, like any native shape.

### What about gradients?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.

# Run a messaging workshop in Google Forms and build a brand style sheet in Google Sheets

*Nov 9, 2026 · svgslid.es blog · Part 2 of the collateral series (part 1: https://svgslid.es/blog/google-slides-collateral-messaging-sheet-gemini)*

## TL;DR
- A messaging workshop runs as a Google Form: 38 questions in 11 sections, built by script from a Workshop tab.
- Answers feed a five-level messaging architecture (primary; context, problem, promise; how; benefits and proof; secondary). Drafts come from =AI(); a person types the approved line.
- The Messages tab gains Role, Source and Source line. Adjunct tabs: Refinements, Audiences, Proof.
- A brand style sheet holds Colors, Type, Layout, Logo, Imagery, Voice, Personality and Gems, and exports itself as one text cell for scripts, agents and Gems.
- Worked example for SVG to Slides: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EOSAfzAkwnhXBWwTkqBSMdMxF-BH9t50
- Starter pack: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12DEX6TnEHQ8goCO29j9ubwYfHP5K72-q

## Workshop sections
Company and focus; market; champion; target organizations; buying scenarios; awareness (1 to 5); needs (must, important, nice); selling proposition (unique, relevant, believable); sweet spot; message raw material; personality and tone (twelve archetypes, four tone scales).

Workshop tab columns: Latest response (newest form row, matched by question text), Override, Final. Everything downstream reads Final.

## Architecture
17 rows on five levels. Each row joins its workshop inputs into Source notes and drafts with the AI function (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/15877199):

    =AI("Promise. Write this element of a B2B messaging hierarchy from the workshop notes. One or two sentences. Plain, specific, active voice.", E6)

Example from our test: Gemini drafted "Convert SVG files into editable vector shapes directly inside Google Slides." The approved lead message is "Editable SVGs in Google Slides."

## Style sheet
Type is set by role (eyebrow, headline, subhead, title, body, stat, label, cta, legal). The Messages tab gives each slot a role; `apply_style.gs` sets font, size and colour on tagged text boxes. The Export tab joins all tabs into one cell of text.

## Gems
Message drafter, copy editor, image maker, image prep, asset checker. Paste the instructions into a Gem, then the export block. Availability depends on your Google plan.

## Test results
- AI formulas written by import or API show as text until you click Generate and fill. One click covers a selected range.
- Our test account hit the monthly AI function limit after five cells.
- Gemini in Slides, on a Workspace account: a single-slide prompt applied three approved lines word for word and kept fonts, sizes and slot tags. The whole-deck prompt was refused; the rollout had not reached the account.
- Gemini in the Slides side panel wrote a 16-element SVG UI mockup to a palette-and-elements brief; it converted to native shapes plus two text boxes without edits. Icons are Phosphor (MIT), placed as native shapes and tagged icon:<key>.
- Sheet formulas and the export block compute. workshop_form.gs built the example form on its first run, on a Workspace account; another account refused the permission request ("This app is blocked"). apply_style.gs and sync_copy.gs have not been run yet.

The screens in the post are mockups. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Forms, Google Drive and Gemini are trademarks of Google LLC.


---

# Update Google Slides collateral from one messaging sheet with Gemini

*Nov 9, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Write the message once in a sheet. Update every one-pager, brief, whitepaper and battlecard from it.

## TL;DR
- Since Oct 30, 2026, Gemini in Google Slides can edit a whole presentation from one prompt, grounded in a Drive file (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/edit-entire-presentations-with-gemini-in-Google-Slides.html).
- Point that prompt at a messaging sheet and one asset updates in one step.
- For exact wording across many assets, tag text boxes with `slot:<key>` in alt text and use a script or an agent.
- Approve the sheet once. Give every slot a character budget. Look at every changed page.
- Starter pack (templates, sheet, prompts, script): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12DEX6TnEHQ8goCO29j9ubwYfHP5K72-q

## What changed
Slides could link charts and tables to Sheets, but not the text in a text box. Gemini's whole-deck editing takes one instruction, decides which slides it applies to, edits them in place as native text and shapes, and lists what it changed. Undo and version history work. Rollout began Oct 29, 2026 and may take longer than 15 days.

## Page sizes
- One-pager, solution brief, whitepaper: 8.5 x 11 in (US Letter) or 21 x 29.7 cm (A4).
- Battlecard: 11 x 8.5 in landscape. Sales deck: Widescreen 16:9.
- File › Page setup › Custom. Units: inches, centimetres, points, pixels. Set size before designing. One size per file.

## Bleed
Slides has no bleed setting. Add the bleed to every side of the canvas (Letter + 0.125 in = 8.75 x 11.25 in). Run colour blocks to the canvas edge, keep text 0.25 in inside the trim, draw trim and safe guides, delete them before export. Ask the printer for their bleed.

## Layout patterns
Six blocks: hero block, three up, proof strip, problem/answer, two columns with pull line, closing strip. Text boxes: fixed size with room to spare, one job per box, one style per role. Logos and icons as vectors (SVG to Slides).

## Messaging sheet
Columns: Key, Fact, Draft, Approved line, Budget, Length, Fits, Used in. Draft can use the Sheets AI function (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/15877199):

    =AI("Write one line of product marketing copy from this fact. Plain, specific, active voice. No superlatives.", B2)

Needs a Google plan with Gemini. Nested AI functions are not supported. Only Approved line reaches an asset.

## Linked tables and charts
Copy in Sheets, paste in Slides, choose Link to spreadsheet. Tools › Linked objects › Update all. Updates are manual. Tables over 400 cells paste unlinked (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/7009814). Updates override edits made in Slides.

## Update one asset with Gemini
Prompt in the Slides side panel, with the sheet referenced:

    Update this presentation from the Approved line column of @Messaging sheet.
    Each row's Used in column says which asset it belongs to.
    Use the approved wording exactly. Do not rephrase, add or remove sentences.
    Keep every layout, font, colour and image as it is.
    Do not add or delete pages.

Limits: Gemini chooses which slides change; one file per prompt; availability depends on rollout and plan.

## Named slots and a script
Right-click a text box › Alt text › Title: `slot:headline`. The key matches the sheet. The pack's Apps Script (`sync_copy.gs`) adds Dry run and Sync copy to assets. Over-budget lines are skipped and flagged. Untagged boxes are never touched. Instruction files for Gemini, Claude and Codex follow one agent contract.

## Approvals
File › Approvals on the sheet (https://support.google.com/drive/answer/9387535). Lock for review. Unlocking during an approval resets approvals; edits after approval leave it attached to the previous version. So: finish words, approve, update assets, lock released assets. Approvals need an eligible work or school account.

## Layout shift
Slides does not shrink text to fit. Budget every slot, fix length in the sheet, skip over-budget lines, look at every changed page, update linked objects last.

## Tested / not tested
Checked: templates keep page sizes and slot tags as Slides files; budget formulas work. The AI function works after a Generate and fill click; our test account hit its monthly limit after five cells. On a Workspace account with Gemini, a single-slide prompt with three approved lines applied them word for word and kept fonts, sizes and slot tags. The whole-deck prompt that references the sheet was refused there ("only able to edit the single currently active slide"); the rollout had not reached the account on Nov 9. The sync script has not been run end to end. Part 2: https://svgslid.es/blog/messaging-workshop-brand-style-sheet-google-sheets

The screens in the post are mockups. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Drive and Gemini are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Google Slides finally does letter spacing

*Nov 7, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Tracking has landed in Google Slides. Here's what it is, how to use it well, and why Docs looks next.

## TL;DR
- Slides now has **letter spacing**, which type designers call **tracking**.
- Toolbar: the **|A|** button next to line spacing. Menu: **Format › Text › Letter spacing**.
- Presets: **6, 3, 0, −1.5**, plus **Custom spacing** (any value, decimals and negatives allowed; no unit shown).
- The Docs help center documents it; the Docs editor doesn't show it yet (as of Nov 7, 2026).

## Tracking vs. kerning vs. leading
- Tracking: same space added/removed after every letter in a selection (the new control).
- Kerning: space between one specific pair (e.g. AV); set by the font, not exposed in Slides.
- Leading: space between lines; the line spacing button.

## Tips
1. Open up all-caps text and small labels (+3 to +6).
2. Tighten large display headlines slightly (−1.5).
3. Leave body text at 0.
4. Bigger type → tighter; smaller type → looser.
5. Positive values widen lines: recheck line breaks and text box overflow.
6. One value per role (eyebrow, headline, body) for consistency.
7. Check in Present mode.

## Steps
1. Select text or a whole text box.
2. Click Letter spacing (|A|) in the toolbar, or Format › Text › Letter spacing.
3. Pick 6, 3, 0 or −1.5. Or choose Custom spacing, enter a value, Apply.
4. Reset by choosing 0.

## The slip-up that points to Docs
- Docs help article "Change how paragraphs & fonts look" (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349) now has an "Adjust letter spacing" section (text, text boxes, tables; toolbar button and Format › Text › Letter spacing).
- Wayback Machine: absent on Oct 5, 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261005194616/https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349?rd=1&visit_id=639268263719815361-3052973569); present Oct 12, 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261012192940/https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349?hl=enGoogle:). Not in July–September captures.
- Docs editor Format › Text menu has no Letter spacing yet (checked Nov 7, 2026).
- Precedent: custom line spacing shipped to Docs and Slides together in Sept 2019 (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2019/09/line-spacing-docs-slides.html).
- No Workspace Updates announcement found yet. Strong signal, not a promise.

# About SVG to Slides

SVG to Slides turns SVG files into native, editable shapes inside Google Slides. Every path becomes its own shape: select it, recolour it with the standard fill picker, resize it without losing quality.

- Three ways in: Chrome extension (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi), web uploader (https://svgslid.es/convert), Google Slides add-on (https://svgslid.es/addon).
- The extension asks for no access to your Google account.
- Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

## Why it exists
Slides has no way to import an SVG; pasted SVGs flatten into images. Where there should be crisp icons and logos, there are crunchy PNGs.

## How it works
SVG to Slides writes Google Slides' own clipboard shape format from your SVG's paths. You paste, and Slides treats the result as native shapes. The extension converts inside your browser.

## Who builds it
Joe Gelman, independently. Contact: joe@glmn.co
